what_its_for: This medicine is used in women who have gone through menopause (when your periods have stopped) to treat moderate to severe hot flashes (sudden feelings of warmth, flushing, or sweating). It also helps protect your bones from getting weak (osteoporosis). It combines two medicines: conjugated estrogens (a type of estrogen hormone) and bazedoxifene (which helps protect the uterus from the effects of estrogen).
how_to_take: Take one tablet by mouth once a day. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or cut it. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not take this medicine with any other estrogen-containing products, progestins, or additional hormone therapies.
dosing: The usual dose is one tablet (containing 0.45 mg conjugated estrogens and 20 mg bazedoxifene) taken by mouth once daily. Your doctor will prescribe the lowest effective dose for the shortest time needed to manage your symptoms. Do not take more than one tablet per day unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on that same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two tablets in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Do not smoke while taking this medicine — smoking increases the risk of serious side effects such as blood clots, stroke, and heart problems. Avoid taking other estrogen products, progestins, or hormonal birth control at the same time. Limit alcohol, as it may increase your risk of breast cancer and other side effects. Avoid prolonged periods of not moving (such as long car or plane trips) which can raise your risk of blood clots. Tell your doctor or dentist about all medications and supplements you take, as some drugs can interfere with how this medicine works.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience any of the following warning signs: sudden chest pain, shortness of breath, or coughing up blood (possible blood clot in the lungs); sudden severe headache, vision changes, weakness on one side of the body, or trouble speaking (possible stroke); pain, swelling, or redness in your leg (possible blood clot); unusual vaginal bleeding; new lumps in your breast; yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); severe stomach or abdominal pain. Also contact your doctor if you notice any new or worsening symptoms, or if your hot flashes do not improve after a few weeks.
when_it_works: Many women begin to notice an improvement in hot flashes within a few weeks of starting this medicine. You may see the most benefit after about 4 to 12 weeks of regular use. Results can vary from person to person. Keep taking it as directed even if you feel better, and talk to your doctor regularly about whether you still need this treatment.
special_populations: This medicine is ONLY for women who have already gone through menopause — it should NOT be used by women who are still having periods, who are pregnant, or who are breastfeeding. It is not approved or safe for use in children or teenagers. Women with a history of blood clots, stroke, heart attack, certain cancers (such as breast or uterine cancer), liver problems, or unexplained vaginal bleeding should NOT take this medicine. Older postmenopausal women may have a higher risk of side effects such as dementia and stroke. Always tell your doctor about all your medical conditions and medications before starting this medicine.
